fact: The civil service ministry's own Direction des Systemes d'Information is charged under decree 2018-38 with keeping SIGFAE running, its data intact, technical support and the civil servants database; the page is undated, so the decree date 2018-01-17 (the document's published date) is used.

SNDI's CEO says the state-owned company, created in 1999, advises, deploys, develops, maintains and trains on ICT networks and tools across all ministries and state institutions, running a nationwide government intranet and VSAT WAN; document published 2014-12-16, no other date given.

SNDI, a state-owned company, says it developed and deployed SIGFIP (public finance) and SIGMAP (public procurement), used nationwide by the Government; document published 2014-12-16, no other date given.

An SNDI representative said at the 25 September 2026 plenary that SNDI has operated its own satellite network since 2006 connecting administrations, universities and health centres, and had provided internet to the University of Korhogo.
RTI Infos describes SNDI as the state's IT operator since 1999, expected to play a larger role in the digital transformation of public administration.

The state company SNDI organised the 21-22 July 2026 seminar and is deploying the interoperability platform for the administration, whose pilot phase covers 12 public bodies; the platform itself is stated to be available (Fraternite Matin, 2026-07-23).

SNDI is stated to have overall charge of executing the interoperability platform project; five administrations had joined it by July 2026, of 12 phase-one bodies, and the SNDI director general says the platform is already available (Digital Mag, 2026-07-22).

SNDI describes itself as the national technical body charged with steering the state's major digitalisation projects, and leads implementation of the interoperability platform for public-administration information systems (SNDI note, 2025-10-01).
The PARAE project document (June 2023), as reported by Sika Finance, says the administration's backup site is hosted at SNDI, the Societe nationale de developpement informatique.
GUCE CI, a state company, manages and maintains the GUCE single-window system, with technical support from the trade ministry.
GUCE CI, a state company (Societe d'Etat), runs the GUCE transaction platform used by ministries' technical services and traders.
GUCE Mobile, with five modules, was launched on 25 July 2024 and was developed and operated entirely by GUCE CI's own teams.
The Société nationale de Développement informatique (SNDI) is the structure in charge of implementing the interoperability platform linking ministries' information systems.
